title: Gaganyaan Orbital Module & Crew Escape System
sourceTitle: ISRO Gaganyaan Mission Overview & Human Spaceflight Centre (HSFC)
summary: Gaganyaan is India's flagship human spaceflight programme designed to demonstrate indigenous human spaceflight capability to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and safe return to Indian territorial waters.
facts: The Gaganyaan Orbital Module comprises the Crew Module (CM) and Service Module (SM) with a total mass of approximately 8,200 kg.
Accommodates a crew of up to three astronauts (Gaganauts) in a 400 km circular low-Earth orbit for a planned 3-day mission duration.
The Crew Module features a thermal protection system, environmental control and life support system (ECLSS), and dual parachute recovery system for splashdown.
Equipped with the Crew Escape System (CES) powered by quick-reacting solid motors capable of autonomous pad-abort and in-flight abort during launch ascent.

title: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram Lander & Pragyan Rover
sourceTitle: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 Mission Details & Lunar Polar Exploration
summary: Chandrayaan-3 is ISRO's successful lunar mission that accomplished historic soft landing in the Moon's South Polar region (Shiv Shakti Point) on August 23, 2023.
facts: Comprises the Vikram Lander (with 4 throttleable liquid engines and hazard detection cameras) and the Pragyan 6-wheeled scientific rover.
Vikram payloads: ChaSTE (thermal probe measuring lunar regolith thermal conductivity), ILSA (seismometer), and RAMBHA-LP (Langmuir probe for lunar plasma).
Pragyan payloads: APXS (Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer) and LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) which confirmed elemental sulfur on the lunar surface.
Propulsion Module served as communications relay and carried the SHAPE payload to study Earth's spectral and polarimetric signatures from lunar orbit.

title: Aditya-L1 Space-based Solar Observatory at Sun-Earth L1
sourceTitle: ISRO Aditya-L1 Solar Mission & Payload Suite
summary: Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated space-based solar observatory positioned in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrangian Point L1 (~1.5 million km from Earth).
facts: Operates from Sun-Earth L1 point providing continuous, uninterrupted observation of the Sun without eclipses or occultations.
Primary payload: Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) designed to image the solar corona and diagnose coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT) captures full-disk images of the solar photosphere and chromosphere in the 200-400 nm UV band.
In-situ instruments ASPEX, PAPA, SoLEXS, HEL1OS, and digital magnetometers measure solar wind protons, alphas, X-ray flares, and interplanetary magnetic fields.

title: Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) Space Station Road-map
sourceTitle: ISRO Vision 2047 & Bharatiya Antariksh Station Architecture
summary: Bharatiya Antariksh Station is India's planned modular space station in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) targeted for initial base module assembly by 2028-2035.
facts: Initial module (BAS-1) mass targeted at ~20-25 tonnes, placed into a ~400-450 km orbit using the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) / LVM3.
Designed to support indigenous microgravity scientific research, astronomy, materials processing, and long-duration human spaceflight physiology.
Features universal docking ports compatible with Gaganyaan crew modules and automated robotic cargo resupply vehicles.
Planned as a stepping stone toward India's national objective of landing an Indian astronaut on the Moon by 2040.

title: Vyommitra AI Robotic Crew Companion
sourceTitle: ISRO HSFC Vyommitra Half-Humanoid Robot for Uncrewed Missions
summary: Vyommitra ('Space Friend') is a female half-humanoid robot developed by ISRO's Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC) and Inertial Systems Unit (IISU) for uncrewed Gaganyaan test flights.
facts: Equipped to monitor environmental parameters, operate switch panels, execute ground-commanded procedures, and simulate human metabolic functions in microgravity.
Features autonomous speech recognition, bilingual conversation capability (Hindi/English), and vision-based switch panel posture recognition.
Designed to measure vibrations, acceleration forces, and acoustic stress during launch and orbital maneuvers to validate crew cabin safety.
Demonstrates human-robot teaming architecture for autonomous habitat maintenance during uncrewed space station intervals.
